correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=3, 0<r<1 and p,q>0 the origin is inside all unit disks for 0<=c<1. In each of n regular angular cells the radial function is rho(c,t)=sqrt(1-c^2 sin^2(t))-c cos(t) for 0<=t<=h=pi/n. Implicit differentiation of rho^2+2c rho cos(t)+c^2=1 gives rho_c<0, rho_t>0, and the exact primitive -rho rho_c=d_t(rho sin t). Outside (c0,c1) the two weighted difference terms are nested and the objective is strictly monotone toward that interval; inside it the unique crossing alpha(c) rises from 0 to h. Direct Leibniz differentiation (zero endpoint integrands at the crossing) yields E_n'(c)=2n((p+q)r sin(alpha(c))-q rho(c,h)sin h). The ratio r sin(alpha(c))/(rho(c,h)sin h) is strictly increasing onto (0,1), so there is exactly one global minimizer for each s=q/(p+q). A uniform Taylor expansion rho=r-delta+[r(1-r)/2]t^2+O(h^4), delta=O(h^2), derives the n^-2 center correction and E_n coefficient pi^3 r^2(1-r)(p+q)s(1-s^2)/3 with O(n^-4) remainder at fixed r,p,q; the expansion does not cover degenerate endpoints r=0,1 or p/q=0. Independent SciPy quadrature/root checks for 18 parameter/n cases corroborate derivative stationarity and scaling, not the infinite proof.
residual_risks: Strict positive p,q; r strictly between zero and one; n>=3; c restricted to [0,1); no arbitrary center-set disk-polygon optimum.
The O(n^-4) remainders fix r,p,q and do not assert uniformity at degenerate weights or radii.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge and restricted to regular-center one-parameter optimization. Primary literature establishes weighted disk-polygon approximation as a natural problem and separately establishes one-sided or fixed-center-radius results, but none inspected gives the precise mixed-sign weighted objective, unique balancing radius for all finite n and fixed positive weights, or sharp O(n^-4) expansion. This is a genuinely narrower theorem than unrestricted disk-polygon approximation, not an assertion of that open problem. Unindexed equivalent calculations remain possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed equal-center-radius balancing or weighted symmetric-difference formula may be equivalent to this theorem.
The primary Basit–Lángi questions address unrestricted disk-n-gons and should not be mistaken for a claim that this broader problem is solved.
The angular-gap area identity and generic analytic differentiation are established techniques; originality is in the full optimized parameter law and asymptotic constant.

value.rationale: Weighted inside/outside area deviation is a mathematically motivated problem raised by primary disk-polygon approximation work. In the canonical rotationally symmetric one-parameter family, a strict global optimum for every finite n and arbitrary positive weights, a weight-interpolating crossing law and an explicit n^-2 curvature/radius coefficient form a reusable comparison benchmark for unrestricted approximation. This is neither a textbook nesting calculation nor an unsupported claim to solve the unrestricted open problem; the nontrivial part is balancing positive area excess and deficit.
residual_risks: Unindexed prior exact symmetric two-sided formulas remain possible.
